photoCapture.label: Photo
photoCapture.hint: PNG, JPG or WEBP, up to 5MB. On a phone, this opens your camera; on a computer, choose an existing photo.
photoCapture.idHelp: Used on your ID/passport and shown to the officer reviewing your application.
photoCapture.wrongType: Please choose a PNG, JPG or WEBP image.
photoCapture.tooLarge: That image is too large — please choose one under 5MB.
photoCapture.required: Please add a photo before submitting.
photoCapture.noFace: We couldn't find a face in that photo. Please choose a clear photo showing your face.
photoCapture.multipleFaces: More than one face was found in that photo. Please choose a photo of yourself alone.
photoCapture.tooFar: Your face is too small in this photo — please move closer or crop in before uploading.
photoCapture.offCenter: Please center your face in the photo before uploading.
photoCapture.blurry: This photo is too blurry. Please hold the camera steady, make sure it's in focus, and retake the photo.
photoCapture.notFacingForward: Please face the camera directly, with your head level and not turned to one side.
photoCapture.busyBackground: The background looks busy or cluttered. Please retake the photo against a plain, even background.
photoCapture.obstructionConfirm: I confirm this photo shows my full face and head clearly, with no hat, sunglasses, or other obstruction.

instructions.title: Photo Capture Instructions
instructions.noHat: Remove any hat, cap, or head covering (an item worn daily for religious reasons is allowed, as long as your full face is clearly visible)
instructions.lookStraight: Look straight at the camera, with a neutral expression and your head level
instructions.plainBackground: Stand against a plain, evenly lit background — not a patterned wall or a cluttered room
instructions.steady: Hold the camera steady so the photo is in focus, not blurry

photoCapture.hat: A hat or cap was detected in that photo. Home Affairs ID photos can't show headwear of any kind — please remove it and retake the photo.
photoCapture.cameraUnavailable: Your camera couldn't be opened on this device — choose an existing photo instead.
photoCapture.cameraFallbackHint: PNG, JPG or WEBP, up to 5MB.
photoCapture.scanInProgressHint: Center your face in the frame, then tap Take photo.
photoCapture.glasses: Eyeglasses, sunglasses or other eyewear were detected in that photo. Home Affairs ID photos can't show eyewear — please remove it and retake the photo.
photoCapture.faceObstruction: Something appears to be covering part of your face (such as a mask, scarf, or hand). Home Affairs ID photos must show your full face clearly — please retake it without anything covering your face.
photoCapture.faceCount: Make sure exactly one person's face is clearly visible in the photo, with nothing else in frame.
photoCapture.unclear: We couldn't clearly verify this photo. Please retake it with your full face visible against a plain background.

biometricCapture.hint: Used to enrol your hand-geometry biometrics for this National ID card.
biometricCapture.scanHint: Place this hand flat and scan it — a real enrolment takes a scan of each hand, not a single photo.
biometricCapture.captureHint: PNG, JPG or WEBP, up to 5MB.
biometricCapture.wrongType: Please choose a PNG, JPG or WEBP image.
biometricCapture.tooLarge: That image is too large — please choose one under 5MB.
biometricCapture.required: A biometric scan of both hands is required before submitting.
biometricCapture.scanInProgressHint: Hold your hand steady in the frame, then tap Capture scan.
biometricCapture.cameraUnavailable: Camera not available on this device — choose an existing image instead.
biometricCapture.noHandDetected: No hand was detected in that scan — make sure an open hand fills most of the frame and try again.
biometricCapture.handTooFar: Your hand is too far from the camera — move it closer and try again.
biometricCapture.handTooClose: Your hand is too close to the camera — move it back slightly and try again.
biometricCapture.tooFewFingersVisible: Not enough fingers were visible in that scan — hold your hand flat and open, fingers spread, and try again.
biometricCapture.enrollWarning: The scan was recorded, but enrolling it against your record failed — you can try again later from your Profile.

signaturePad.required: Please have the citizen sign before confirming.

auth.usernameOrEmailHelp: Enter your username, or the email address on your account if you have one.
auth.emailOptionalHelp: Optional — you do not need an email to use this system.
auth.alreadyHaveAccount: Already have an account? Log in
auth.dontHaveAccount: Don't have an account? Create one
auth.chooseIdentityOption: Do you already have a permanent identity number?
auth.needToRegister: No, I don't have one yet
auth.identityNotFound: No matching identity record was found. Check your permanent identity number and date of birth.
auth.provisionalNotice: A provisional account is not a verified identity. It lets you begin a Home Affairs identity process and track it, but most services remain locked until your identity is verified.
auth.provisionalNoticeShort: Provisional account — identity not yet verified
auth.changePasswordSubtitle: Set a new password for your account
auth.mustChangePasswordNotice: You're using a temporary password. You must set your own password before you can continue.
auth.passwordTooShort: New password must be at least 8 characters.
auth.notACitizen: No, I am not a Lesotho citizen
auth.foreignNationalNotice: A foreign-national account has no access to government services yet. You can apply for Citizenship by Naturalization under Home Affairs once you have lived in Lesotho for at least 5 years — full access unlocks once that application is approved.
auth.foreignNationalNoticeShort: Foreign national — citizenship not yet granted
auth.securityQuestionsHelp: Choose two different questions and answer both. If you ever forget your password, you'll use these to get back into your account — there is no email link, since email is optional.
auth.securityQuestionsRequired: Choose two security questions and answer both.

securityQuestions.mothersMaidenName: What is your mother's maiden name?
securityQuestions.firstSchool: What was the name of your first school?
securityQuestions.firstPetName: What was the name of your first pet?
securityQuestions.birthVillage: What is the name of the village or town where you were born?
securityQuestions.favoriteTeacher: What was the name of your favorite teacher?

auth.forgotPasswordUsernameIntro: Enter your username and we'll ask your two security questions to confirm it's you.
auth.forgotPasswordAnswersIntro: Answer both security questions you set when you created your account.
auth.forgotPasswordAnswersCorrect: Verified — you can now set a new password.
auth.forgotPasswordDone: Your password has been changed. You can now log in with your new password.

birthRegistrationForm.title: Apply for a birth certificate
birthRegistrationForm.automaticNotice: Your application is checked automatically against the Home Affairs civil register and approved or rejected immediately — there is no officer review queue.
birthRegistrationForm.parentInfoReused: Your verified information as parent/guardian has been reused from your Home Affairs record — you do not need to re-enter it.
birthRegistrationForm.isCitizen: Is this parent a Lesotho citizen?
birthRegistrationForm.identityNumberHelp: Checked automatically against the Home Affairs civil register — the application is rejected immediately if there is no match.
birthRegistrationForm.chiefLetterHelp: Where applicable — upload a photo or scan of the original letter from the chief.
birthRegistrationForm.chiefLetterStampNotice: The letter must clearly show the chief's official stamp. An application with a letter that has no visible stamp cannot be processed, so please check this before uploading.
birthRegistrationForm.proofOfBirthHelp: Upload a photo or scan of the original birth record, clinical booklet, or baptismal certificate.
birthRegistrationForm.marriageCertificateHelp: Where applicable — upload a photo or scan of the original certificate.
birthRegistrationForm.acknowledgementOfPaternityHelp: Where applicable — upload a photo or scan of the original document.

birthRegistrationForm.parentStatusUnknownHelp: Nothing further is required if this parent is genuinely unknown.
birthRegistrationForm.parentStatusAbsentHelp: Optional — only if the name is known. Nothing else is required.
birthRegistrationForm.parentStatusDeceasedHelp: Optional. If given, it will be checked against our deceased records.

birthCertificateApplicationForm.title: Apply for your birth certificate
birthCertificateApplicationForm.intro: If you don't yet have a Lesotho permanent identity number, use this form to apply for your own birth certificate. This is the first step before you can create an account — you don't need to be logged in.
birthCertificateApplicationForm.approvedBody: Your permanent identity number is {{pin}}. Your birth certificate ({{certificateNumber}}) has been generated.

nationalIdForm.title: Apply for a National ID card
nationalIdForm.eligibleNotice: You are eligible to apply for a National ID card.
nationalIdForm.reuseNotice: Your name, date of birth, sex, place of birth and permanent identity number are reused from your verified Home Affairs record.
nationalIdForm.noNewNumberNotice: Your existing permanent identity number will be used. A new number is never issued.
nationalIdForm.biometricCaptureHelp: Choose the police station where you will visit in person to have both hands scanned. This is captured only once — it will be reused automatically for every service that needs it in future.
nationalIdForm.biometricsOnFile: You already have biometrics on file from an earlier service — no police-station visit is needed. Your card will be approved automatically on submission.
nationalIdForm.policeStationRequired: Choose the police station where you will have your biometrics captured.
nationalIdForm.tooYoung: You must be at least {{minimumAge}} years old to apply for a National ID card (you are {{age}}).

nationalIdForm.alreadyHaveCard: You have already obtained a National ID card. Use the renewal or replacement service instead.
nationalIdForm.submittedAwaitingBiometrics: Please visit the police station you chose to have your biometrics captured — your card will be approved and sent for production automatically once that's done.
nationalIdForm.submittedAutoApproved: Your biometrics were already on file, so your card has been approved automatically and sent for production.

correctionForm.title: Report an error in your civil record

marriageForm.title: Register a Marriage
marriageForm.filerInfoReused: Your own verified identity is used automatically as one spouse's particulars — you don't need to re-enter it.
marriageForm.spousePermanentIdHelp: If your spouse already has a national identity number, entering it helps link the records. Leave blank if not known.
marriageForm.certifyIntro: is to certify that the marriage described above was registered in accordance with the laws of the Kingdom of Lesotho.
marriageForm.certifiedStatement: This certifies that the marriage described above was registered in accordance with the laws of the Kingdom of Lesotho.

divorceForm.title: Register a Divorce
divorceForm.courtNotice: A Lesotho court grants a divorce — Home Affairs registers it against that court order. You will need the court order reference.
divorceForm.marriageReferenceHelp: If the marriage was registered in this system, enter its certificate number. Otherwise, leave blank.
divorceForm.divorceOrderDate: Date the court granted the divorce
divorceForm.certifiedStatement: This certifies that the divorce described above, granted by the court named, has been registered in accordance with the laws of the Kingdom of Lesotho.

deathForm.intro: Anyone can report a death for registration. You will need the deceased’s permanent identity number.
deathForm.deceasedPermanentIdHelp: This is the deceased's own national identity number, on their National ID card.
deathForm.submitted: Death registration for {{name}} has been submitted and is awaiting review.
deathForm.officerIntro: Review and approve death registrations. Approving marks the citizen record as deceased and issues the death certificate automatically.

birthCertificateReissueForm.intro: Request a new copy of your birth certificate if the original was lost, damaged, or never collected.
birthCertificateReissueForm.doesNotExpireNotice: A birth certificate does not expire, so this is not a renewal — it only replaces a copy that was lost, damaged, or never collected. You must state your reason and upload proof supporting it (for example a police report for a lost certificate, or a photo of a damaged one).

field.birthRecordIdHelp: The reference number of your approved birth registration (see your birth certificate or My Applications).
field.proofHelp: Upload evidence supporting your reason — e.g. a police report for a lost certificate, or a photo of the damaged one.

deathCertificateView.title: Death Certificate
deathCertificateView.demoNotice: Demo document — for prototype/testing purposes only. Not a legal record.
deathCertificateView.notReadyMessage: This certificate has not been approved yet, so there is nothing to view. Check back once the request has been approved.
deathCertificateView.certifiedStatement: This certifies that the particulars above are recorded as an entry in the Register of Deaths maintained by the Ministry of Home Affairs.

nameChangeForm.intro: Request a formal, legal change of your first name or surname (for example after marriage, divorce, or by personal choice).

adoptionForm.intro: Register a court-ordered adoption so Home Affairs updates the child's guardian on record.

field.childIdHelp: The permanent identity number already on the child's citizen record.

solemnisationForm.intro: Book the marriage ceremony itself — a date, branch and officiant — separately from registering a marriage that has already taken place.

marriageOfficersForm.intro: Register and manage the people authorised to perform civil, religious or traditional marriages.
marriageOfficersForm.officerOnly: This page is for Home Affairs officers only.

nationalIdRenewReplaceForm.intro: Apply to renew an expired National ID card, or replace one that was lost, stolen or damaged.

field.replacementProofHelp: Upload evidence supporting your reason — e.g. a police report for a lost or stolen card, or a photo of the damaged one.

nationalIdRenewReplaceForm.photoReused: No new photo is needed — the photo already on file with your current ID is reused automatically.
nationalIdRenewReplaceForm.noCardFound: No collected National ID card was found on your record. Use the standard National ID Application for a first-time card.
nationalIdRenewReplaceForm.notYetExpiredNotice: Your current card is not yet expired — it expires on {{expiryDate}}. Renewal is only available once it has expired.
nationalIdRenewReplaceForm.waitNotice: A {{months}}-month wait applies before a lost/stolen card can be replaced. You will be able to apply from {{date}}.
nationalIdRenewReplaceForm.waitPassedNotice: The {{months}}-month wait has passed — you can submit this replacement.

naturalizationForm.title: Apply for Citizenship by Naturalization
naturalizationForm.intro: If you are a foreign national who has lived in Lesotho for at least 5 years, you may apply to become a citizen of Lesotho. A Home Affairs officer will review your application and supporting documents.
naturalizationForm.notApplicable: This service is for foreign-national accounts applying to become citizens of Lesotho. It does not apply to your account.
naturalizationForm.eligibilityNotice: You must have lived in Lesotho for at least 5 years before you can apply, supported by a letter from your area chief confirming your residency. Studying or working in Lesotho on a Work Permit or Study Permit does not by itself qualify you — see Citizenship by Registration if you are married to a Lesotho citizen instead.
naturalizationForm.feeNotice: A naturalization application fee is payable. Upload your payment reference and a photo of the receipt.

field.arrivalDate: Date you arrived to live in Lesotho
field.arrivalDateHelp: Used to confirm you meet the 5-year residency requirement.
field.chiefLetterHelp: A letter from the chief of the area where you live, confirming how long you have lived there — required as proof of the arrival date above.
field.chiefLetterRequired: A chief's letter confirming your residency is required.

naturalizationQueue.title: Citizenship by Naturalization Applications
naturalizationQueue.desc: Review foreign-national applications for citizenship, including each applicant's chief's letter and supporting documents.
naturalizationQueue.empty: No naturalization applications waiting for review.

marriageCitizenshipForm.title: Apply for Citizenship by Registration (Marriage to a Lesotho Citizen)
marriageCitizenshipForm.intro: If you are married to a citizen of Lesotho, you may be entitled to be registered as a citizen under section 40 of the Constitution (as amended in 2018), after five years of cohabitation and continuous lawful stay in Lesotho together — or, if your spouse has since died, five years of continuous lawful stay alone. A Home Affairs officer will review your application against your marriage record.
marriageCitizenshipForm.notApplicable: This service is for foreign-national accounts applying to become citizens of Lesotho through marriage to a Lesotho citizen. It does not apply to your account.
marriageCitizenshipForm.eligibilityNotice: You must reference an already-approved marriage certificate issued by Home Affairs, and show at least five years of cohabitation and continuous lawful stay in Lesotho with your spouse (or, if your spouse has since died, five years of continuous lawful stay alone).
marriageCitizenshipForm.feeNotice: A registration application fee is payable. Upload your payment reference and a photo of the receipt.

field.marriageCertificateNumberHelp: The certificate number from your approved Home Affairs marriage registration, e.g. MC-2026-483920.
field.lastNameHelp: Must match the name recorded for you on the marriage certificate above.
field.arrivalDate: Date you arrived to live in Lesotho
field.arrivalDateHelp: Used to confirm your continuous lawful stay in Lesotho.
field.cohabitationStartDate: Date you began living together with your spouse in Lesotho
field.cohabitationStartDateHelp: Not required if your spouse has since died — leave blank in that case.

marriageCitizenshipQueue.title: Citizenship by Registration Applications
marriageCitizenshipQueue.desc: Review applications from foreign nationals married to a Lesotho citizen, each checked against an approved Home Affairs marriage record.
marriageCitizenshipQueue.empty: No citizenship by registration applications waiting for review.

homeAffairs.birthCertificatesIntro: View your own birth certificate and any of your children's, and request a reissue if one is lost, damaged, or never collected.
homeAffairs.birthCertificatesEmpty: You don't have a birth certificate on file yet, and no children are registered under your account.

parentConfirmations.title: Parentage confirmations
parentConfirmations.intro: You've been named as a parent on a birth registration. Review it below and confirm or dispute it — this never affects a certificate that has already been issued.
parentConfirmations.empty: You have no pending parentage confirmations.
parentConfirmations.confirmHelp: Sign below to confirm you are this child's parent, as named on this registration.
parentConfirmations.disputeReasonRequired: A reason is required to dispute this.
parentConfirmations.signatureRequired: A signature is required to confirm.

parentageDisputesForm.title: Parentage disputes
parentageDisputesForm.intro: The other named parent has disputed a birth registration. This is the only point in the birth-certificate process where an officer is involved.
parentageDisputesForm.empty: There are no open parentage disputes.
parentageDisputesForm.awaitingCorrectionNotice: This dispute was upheld — the parent has been cleared from the record and the certificate flagged for correction. The applicant and the disputing parent were told to visit a Home Affairs office. Once they have discussed it with you in person, enter the correct parent details below.

passport.title: Passport Services
passport.feeNotice: The passport fee must be paid before you apply — enter your payment reference and attach a photo of your receipt.

subject.label: Who is this passport for?

subject.chooseSomeone: Choose who this application is for.

subject.childInProgress: This child already has a passport application in progress.
subject.selfInProgress: You already have a passport application in progress.
subject.idRequired: You must already hold a National ID card before applying for a passport. Please apply for your National ID first.

renewal.pagesFullDeclaration: This passport's pages are full and it needs to be renewed even though it hasn't expired yet.
renewal.surrenderNotice: You will need to bring your original passport to the office so an officer can verify it in person before this application can be completed. It will not be approved without this.

field.confirmPassportNumberHelp: Type the passport number printed inside your current passport.
field.pageCount: How many pages does your passport have?
field.lastPageProofHelp: Take a clear photo right now of the last page of your passport, showing it is fully used.

surrender.failedModalHelp: This rejects the application. If the citizen's passport is genuinely lost or stolen, tell them to apply through Passport Replacement instead.
surrender.awaitingNotice: Bring your original passport to the office. Once an officer has checked it and your payment together, your new passport will be produced right away.
surrender.verifiedNotice: The original passport has been received and verified.

traffic.title: Traffic
traffic.hubIntro: Driving licences, vehicle registration and transport permit services.

field.existingLicenceNumberHelp: A Public Driving Permit is issued against a driving licence you already hold — it does not replace it.

field.chassisNumberHelp: Uniquely identifies the vehicle and prevents duplicate registration.
field.ownershipProofHelp: A photo of the purchase receipt, bill of sale, or ownership document.

vehicleRegistrationForm.title: Vehicle Registration

field.preferredOffice: Traffic office you will bring the vehicle to

vehicleRegistrationForm.physicalInspectionNotesLabel: Any other observations (vehicle condition, discrepancies, etc.)
vehicleRegistrationForm.physicalInspectionNotice: Once submitted, bring the vehicle to your chosen traffic office. An officer must physically inspect it and confirm the chassis and engine numbers before your registration can be approved.
vehicleRegistrationForm.customsVerificationNotesLabel: What did you check? (customs clearance, VAT/import tax proof, police clearance)
vehicleRegistrationForm.categoryGuideBody: Choose "Vehicle Registration" for a brand-new vehicle bought in Lesotho. Choose "Vehicle Registration (Imported/SADC)" for a brand-new vehicle imported into Lesotho. Choose "Vehicle Registration (Second-Hand Imported)" for a second-hand vehicle imported into Lesotho. For an imported vehicle, you must first complete customs clearance with Revenue Services Lesotho (RSL) before applying here — RSL operates outside this platform, so this system cannot contact them for you.
vehicleRegistrationForm.changeOfOwnershipNotice: Already registering a second-hand vehicle that's already registered in Lesotho, and just changing the owner on record?
vehicleRegistrationForm.officerChassisNumberLabel: Chassis number you see on the vehicle
vehicleRegistrationForm.officerEngineNumberLabel: Engine number you see on the vehicle

field.originCountry: Country the vehicle was imported from
field.importProofHelp: A photo of the import/customs document or purchase receipt.
field.customsClearanceHelp: The reference number from your customs clearance certificate.
field.importTaxProof: Proof of import VAT / tax payment
field.importTaxProofHelp: A photo of your VAT/import duty payment receipt.
field.policeClearanceHelp: A photo of your CID/Interpol/SARPCC police clearance confirming the vehicle is not reported stolen.
field.customsClearanceDocumentHelp: A photo of the actual customs clearance certificate from RSL — not just the reference number.

field.transferProofHelp: A photo of the signed sale agreement or transfer document.

numberPlateForm.title: Vehicle Number Plate

field.personalisedTextHelp: Required only if your reason is ‘Personalised’.

numberPlateForm.newPlateAutoNotice: A brand new plate is no longer requested here — it is generated automatically once your Temporary Permit (issued when your vehicle registration is approved) expires after 21 days. Use this form only for a lost, damaged, or personalised plate.

field.insuranceProofHelp: A photo of your current certificate of insurance.

testBookingsForm.intro: A Theory test requires an approved Learner Permit. A Practical test additionally requires a passed Theory test.
testBookingsForm.introNew: Book your theory test. It is scheduled automatically for the date you choose - there is no waiting for an officer to confirm it. Once you pass, your practical test is auto-requested for the following day; an officer will then confirm its exact date, time and location.
testBookingsForm.introOfficer: Publish one shared set of multiple-choice questions for each day's theory sitting at your office — citizens are notified and mark their own test automatically. A practical sitting still needs an officer to confirm its date, time and location before it's scheduled, and its result recorded by hand. Either kind of sitting can be postponed if needed.
testBookingsForm.autoScheduleHelp: Your test is confirmed for this date as soon as you submit - no further waiting.
testBookingsForm.theoryAlreadyBooked: You already have a theory test booked. It will show in the table below.
testBookingsForm.autoScheduled: Your theory test is confirmed for {{date}}.
testBookingsForm.schedulePracticalIntro: This sets ONE date, start time and venue for every citizen below who's waiting on their practical test at your office — it applies to all {{count}} of them at once, so nobody can be given a different date, time or venue than the rest. Everyone affected will be notified.
testBookingsForm.schedulePracticalCount: {{count}} citizen(s) waiting to have their practical test scheduled.
testBookingsForm.schedulePracticalNone: No practical tests are waiting to be scheduled right now.
testBookingsForm.schedulePracticalDone: Scheduled the practical test for {{count}} citizen(s).
testBookingsForm.awaitingSchedule: Awaiting officer to confirm date, time & location
testBookingsForm.awaitingBulkSchedule: Awaiting the office's next bulk practical-test scheduling
testBookingsForm.postponeIntro: Move this test to a new date (and time, if needed) — for example because of bad weather. The citizen will be notified.

instructorsForm.officerOnly: This registry is managed by Traffic officers only.
instructorsForm.intro: Certification of driving instructors and practical test examiners.

learnerPermitStatus.intro: Your Learner's Permit is issued automatically once you pass your theory and practical driving tests - there is nothing to apply for here.
learnerPermitStatus.officerIntro: Every Learner's Permit issued, system-generated on a passed practical test. There is nothing to action here.
learnerPermitStatus.noneYet: You don't hold a Learner's Permit yet. Book and pass your theory test, then your practical test, to earn one.

drivingLicence.title: Driving Licence
drivingLicence.inProgress: You already have a driving licence application in progress.

help.walkthroughIntro: Every service on this portal follows roughly the same five steps.

walkthroughSteps.title: Create an account
walkthroughSteps.desc: An existing citizen verifies with their permanent identity number and date of birth. Someone without a civil record yet applies for a birth certificate first. A foreign national registers and gets a provisional account that unlocks once their citizenship application is approved.

walkthroughSteps.title: Verify your identity
walkthroughSteps.desc: Your account is checked against your official civil record. Until that's confirmed (or, for a foreign national, until citizenship is approved), you'll see a notice guiding you to the right application instead of the full portal.

walkthroughSteps.title: Apply for a service
walkthroughSteps.desc: Choose a department from your dashboard, open the service you need, and complete its form — most ask for supporting documents, a photo, or in some cases a hand-biometric scan.

walkthroughSteps.title: Track your application
walkthroughSteps.desc: Every application you submit appears under “My Applications” with its current status. If an officer needs more from you, you'll get a notification and a chance to resubmit.

walkthroughSteps.title: Collect or receive your result
walkthroughSteps.desc: Depending on the service, you'll either collect a physical document at your nearest branch office, or the result (like a digital certificate) becomes available directly in your account.

help.faqIntro: Grouped by topic — use the search box above to jump straight to one.

faq.q: I'm a Lesotho citizen but I don't have a permanent identity number yet. How do I register?
faq.a: On the registration page, choose “I need to register”. That takes you to the public birth certificate application — once Home Affairs approves it, you're guided straight into creating your account with your new identity number.

faq.q: I'm not a Lesotho citizen — can I use this portal?
faq.a: Yes. Choose “I'm not a citizen” on the registration page. You'll get a provisional account that unlocks the full portal once you successfully apply for citizenship — either by naturalization, or by registration if you're married to a Lesotho citizen.
Use “Forgot password” on the login page and answer the two security questions you set up when you created your account.

faq.q: What is my permanent identity number?
faq.a: A unique number tied to your civil record, used across every department. You can see a masked version on your dashboard — tap it to reveal the full number, or find it on your Profile page.

faq.q: How do I check the status of an application?
faq.a: Open “My Applications” from the main menu. Every application you've ever submitted, across every department, is listed there with its current status.

faq.q: An officer asked for more information — what do I do?
faq.a: You'll get a notification and the application's status changes to “Additional Information Required.” Open it from My Applications to see exactly what's missing, then resubmit from the same screen.

faq.q: Can I apply for more than one service at a time?
faq.a: Yes — applications from different services and departments are completely independent of each other.

faq.q: Why does a service ask me to scan my hand or take a photo?
faq.a: Certain services — like a National ID, a Driving Licence, or a citizenship application — require a hand-biometric scan or a photo as part of your official record, the same way a physical ID card requires a photo and fingerprint today.

faq.q: How do I pay for a service?
faq.a: Most paid services ask you to pay at the relevant office or an approved payment channel first, then enter the payment reference and upload a photo of your receipt as part of the application.
Only you, and the officers at the specific department your application concerns. System administrators can access records for platform administration. See our Privacy Policy for the full picture.

Your account is protected by a password and security questions, and sensitive civil records are only edited by verified officers. See our Privacy Policy for details on what's collected and how it's used.

help.departmentGuidesIntro: A quick overview of what each department covers and the typical path through its services.

home_affairs.intro: Home Affairs handles your civil identity — birth, marriage, divorce and death registration, National ID, passports, name changes, adoption and citizenship.
steps: Open Home Affairs from your dashboard.
Pick the service you need — e.g. National ID Application or Birth Registration.
Complete the form and upload the required photo or documents.
Some services, like National ID, need a biometric capture at a branch office before approval.
Track progress in My Applications, then collect your document or view it digitally once approved.

traffic.intro: Traffic covers driving licences, vehicle registration, transport permits, and the tests and inspections that go with them.
steps: Open Traffic from your dashboard.
For a driving licence, you'll usually book and pass a theory test, then a practical test, before applying.
For a vehicle, register it under Vehicle Registration — this can require a physical inspection and customs verification.
Track every application and test booking under My Applications and Appointments.

finance.intro: Finance services require a verified citizen identity and cover government employment records, supplier payments, retirement tracking, and budget/tender publications.
steps: Open Finance from your dashboard and choose the relevant service.
If something seems wrong with a payment or process in any department, use “Report a Financial Issue” from your dashboard's quick actions — not the department itself.

pensions.intro: Pensions services let you verify and check on pension beneficiary status.
steps: Open Pensions from your dashboard.
Submit a Pension Enquiry with the beneficiary's details.
Track the result in My Applications.

police.intro: Police services include identity verification, Police Clearance Certificates, and reporting crimes, lost or stolen property, missing persons and other incidents.
steps: Open Police from your dashboard.
For a Police Clearance Certificate, apply and wait for review — some cases require biometric verification.
To report an incident, choose the matching report type (lost property, stolen property, general crime, cybercrime, missing person, domestic violence, or traffic accident).
Track any case reference under Police Case Track.

passport.intro: Passport services are grouped under Home Affairs and cover new applications, renewals and page-related changes.
steps: Open Passport (listed under Home Affairs).
Apply and upload the required documents and photo.
Some passport services require in-person verification or surrender of an old document.
Collect your passport once it's ready.

help.stillNeedHelpDesc: If none of this answered your question, Contact Us — or, if it's about a specific application, its own page usually has the most up-to-date information.

about.intro: Integrated Government Services brings Lesotho's government departments — Home Affairs, Traffic, Finance, Pensions, Police and Passport Services — into one citizen account, instead of a separate queue, form and office for each one.

sections.heading: One citizen, one profile
sections.body: Your identity is verified once, against your civil record, and then recognised across every department. You don't re-enter your personal details for each new application.

sections.heading: Why it exists
sections.body: Many government services currently require an in-person visit just to check a status or submit a routine form. This portal aims to move as much of that online as the service genuinely allows — while keeping the parts that legitimately need an officer's judgement, like biometric capture or document verification, in the hands of a real officer.

sections.heading: Built transparently
sections.body: Every application you submit is tracked with a visible status, every status change is logged, and officer-facing review queues work the same way across every department — so the process behind a decision is consistent, not ad-hoc.

sections.heading: A prototype in active development
sections.body: This system is a prototype, built and maintained as an ongoing development project rather than a finished product. Features are added and refined over time; if something looks incomplete, it likely is — and that's expected at this stage.

contactPage.intro: For anything about a specific application or service, the fastest answers are usually inside the portal itself.

channels.title: Check the Help Centre first
channels.body: Most questions about how a service works are already answered there, organised by topic.

channels.title: Application-specific updates
channels.body: If an officer needs more information from you, you'll be notified directly inside the portal — check Notifications and My Applications before looking elsewhere.

channels.title: A problem with a payment or financial process
channels.body: Use “Report a Financial Issue” from your dashboard's quick actions. It reaches the right department directly, whichever one it concerns.

channels.title: In person
channels.body: For matters that genuinely can't be resolved online, visit the branch office that handles the relevant department's services in your district.

contactPage.prototypeNote: This portal is a prototype. A production deployment would list real department phone numbers, email addresses and office hours here; for now, the channels above are the ones this demonstration system actually supports.

privacyPolicy.intro: This page describes what information this portal collects and how it's used.

sections.heading: What we collect
sections.body: Your identity details (name, date of birth, permanent identity number), contact information, your account credentials and security question answers, and — for specific services — hand-biometric templates, photos, and documents you upload (such as receipts or supporting evidence).

sections.heading: How we use it
sections.body: To process the specific application or service you submit, to verify your identity against your civil record, to let the reviewing officers at the relevant department act on your request, and to maintain the record-keeping and audit trail government services require.

sections.heading: Who can see it
sections.body: Only you, and the officers at the specific department your application concerns. System administrators can access records for platform administration and support, not for unrelated departments' day-to-day work.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
sections.body: Civil records (birth, marriage, National ID and similar) are retained as part of your permanent government record. Application-specific documents are kept as long as needed to process and audit that application.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: You can view your own civil record and application history at any time through your account. If something in your record is wrong, the relevant department's Correction service is the way to request a fix.

sections.heading: About this policy
sections.body: This portal is a prototype under active development. This page reflects what the current system actually does; a production deployment would carry a full legal and security review beyond what's described here.

termsOfUse.intro: By creating an account and using this portal, you agree to the following.

sections.heading: Accurate information
sections.body: You agree to provide accurate information and to use the portal only for your own legitimate government service needs. Knowingly submitting false information on an application — for example a birth, marriage, or identity application — may result in the application being rejected and your account reviewed.

sections.heading: Your account
sections.body: Keep your password and security question answers confidential. You're responsible for activity carried out under your account.

sections.heading: Availability
sections.body: Government services depend on officer review and are not instant. The portal shows a system status indicator, but availability isn't guaranteed at all times.

sections.heading: Changes
sections.body: These terms, and the services available on this portal, may change as the system develops.

sections.heading: About these terms
